defects.defect: CORE-54: WordList (core/word-hints.ts) is no package export and is built only from the program's static lists (BIP39 English, Bytewords). Its constructor still refuses bad lists with three core.word-hints.* codes, and word-hints-self-test.ts passes a sparse list on purpose. This guards against a failure nobody can cause.
defects.how: The word lists are static data compiled in; forms::hints takes a &'static [&'static str] and has no list-shape refusals (CORE-54), and its self-test feeds no malformed list.

defects.defect: CORE-54: core.pieces.piece-whole-width-at-least-1 guards piece widths that are always program constants.
defects.how: Piece widths are constants of each form entry; no run-time guard.

defects.defect: CORE-54: EncodedBackup.words asserts again the word count its constructor already checked. ReEncoding's constructor catch and its #result view check again (ownedDates) the dates the library decoded itself, and wipe on a failure no input can cause.
defects.how: A validated Phrase and an EncodedBackup are built once and carry their count by type; ReEncoding holds the library's own decoded values without re-checks or a catch that wipes on an impossible failure.

defects.defect: CORE-54 (shared module used by every catalog of this domain): ErrorCatalog.create checks at run time for an unknown code or a message that is not text, although both come from static, typed program data.
defects.how: Codes are enum variants with a code() match and a Display impl per module; an unknown code or a non-text message cannot be written, so there is no run-time catalog check.

defects.defect: CORE-23: MissingChecksumError (core/masking.ts) is the domain's only refusal outside an ErrorCatalog. Its code 'missing-checksum' has no namespace, unlike every other code.
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: the code gets the core.masking namespace inside the modes error enum (CORE-23); the wallet-tools session is told.

defects.defect: CORE-23: words.ts and word-table.ts each build an ErrorCatalog with the same namespace 'core.words'. Code uniqueness across the two modules holds only by convention.
defects.how: Each module has its own enum; a test over the refusal known-answer file (vectors/ts-0.1.0/refusals-v1.json) checks that every code across all enums is unique.

defects.defect: CORE-23: in re-encode-command.ts, phraseEndingWith recognises the refusal by comparing error.message with NO_SUCH_LAST_WORD instead of using its code core.re-encoding.no-such-last-word.
defects.how: The front end matches the refusal's variant (ReEncodingError::NoSuchLastWord), never its message.

defects.defect: Code naming: core.dates.assert-calendar-date-refused and assert-calendar-date-refused-2 stand for 'year out of range' and 'month out of range', but their names do not say which, so a host cannot choose its words by the code.
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: core.dates.year-out-of-range and core.dates.month-out-of-range, variants YearOutOfRange and MonthOutOfRange; the wallet-tools session is told.

defects.defect: One code covers two conditions: bitsToBytes refuses both a length that is not a multiple of 8 and a character other than 0/1 with core.bits.entropy-contain-whole-number-bytes. This goes against the catalog's own 'two conditions take two codes' rule, and its input always comes from the program's own bit strings.
defects.how: Entropy comes from the bip39 crate (to_entropy_array of a validated phrase) into a fixed owner; no 0/1 strings exist, so the condition and its code cannot occur and are dropped.

defects.defect: Inconsistent trimming: parseDate, isDatePattern, parseDatePattern, WordTable.lookup, serializeRecord/parseRecord and re-encode's last-word file use String.prototype.trim. white-space.ts makes trimWhiteSpace the one rule, and the two differ on U+FEFF and U+0085.
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: one rule everywhere, Unicode White_Space at the ends (TS trimWhiteSpace, Rust str::trim), written once in text::.

defects.defect: Secret hygiene: seedshift.ts moves entropy through '0'/'1' JavaScript strings (bitsOfIndexes, bytesToBits, shiftedEntropyBits) that cannot be wiped. Every read of EncodedBackup.indexes also returns a fresh frozen copy that cannot be wiped. A Rust version should keep entropy and indexes in zeroizing buffers and lend them by reference.
defects.how: Entropy, indexes and shifted entropy live in SecretBytes owners (locked, zeroized) and are lent by reference; no fresh copies per read.

defects.defect: The compatibility exports decodeInput, decodeInputLegacy and decodeInputDirect do not wipe the index arrays they parse, unlike EncodedBackup.read.
defects.how: There are no compatibility decode entries in Rust: one decode path, whose index arrays sit in a secret owner.

defects.defect: EncodedBackup.shorterPhrases catches and drops every error of a shorter start (catch {} return []), wiped-secret refusals included. CORE-22 says no error is swallowed.
defects.how: shorter_phrases returns Result: only the expected 'not a phrase' outcome becomes an empty list; every other error passes on (CORE-22).

defects.defect: EncodedForm.cardCodes does not hold its indexes to assertPhraseIndexes, while codes() and elements() do.
defects.how: Card codes are written from the validated Phrase's indexes, which cannot hold an out-of-range index.

defects.defect: Color Unicode reading uses two separator rules: the hex path splits at white space, commas, semicolons and #, but the symbol path (colorUnicodePoints, colorSymbolsOf) drops white space only, so Private Use symbols separated by commas are refused.
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: one separator rule for both paths of forms::color_unicode (white space, commas, semicolons and #).

defects.defect: record.unsupported-mode is raised only by serializeRecord. parseRecord reports an unknown mode in a header as record.malformed-header, but an unknown format as record.unsupported-format.
defects.how: serialize takes a Mode value, so an unsupported mode cannot be written and that path's code is gone; parse keeps record.malformed-header and record.unsupported-format as TS 0.1.0.

defects.defect: Front ends differ: EncodedForm.alwaysMasked (forms 1 and 2) is enforced only by the menu. 'encode --mode direct --format 1|2' is accepted on the command line.
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: the library refuses --mode direct with forms 1 and 2 for every front end, before any secret; the wallet-tools session is told.

defects.defect: In the library, Masking.of('seedshift-legacy-valid').encode works, although the mode is not encodable and EncodedBackup.assertEncodable refuses it.
defects.how: Only encodable modes have an encode method (a separate EncodableMode type), so the library cannot encode in seedshift-legacy-valid.

defects.defect: The message 'Unicode code N is not a BIP39 word.' (core.words.unicode-code-not-bip39-word) puts the code's place where a reader expects the code, so it reads as if N were the code.
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: the message names the place as a place ('The Unicode code at place N is not a BIP39 word.').

defects.defect: Misleading comments: self-test-vectors.ts and re-encoding-self-test.ts say the Unicode codes come from bip-0039/chinese_simplified.txt, while WordTable uses the Traditional Chinese list. The answers happen to match for 的 and 在, and MANUAL_RECOVERY.md forbids substituting the Simplified list.
defects.how: Comments and the known-answer provenance name the Traditional Chinese list, which word_table/chinese_traditional.rs holds.

defects.defect: The task names a package entry 'mnemocode/core', but package.json has no such export. src/core.ts is reachable only through 'mnemocode'.
defects.how: Library paths are crate modules named in ARCHITECTURE.md's module map; the binding exposes one module per part.

defects.defect: Bitcoin address evidence whose type is in none of the selected --bitcoin-profile values is accepted by assertWalletEvidence and can never match. Confirmed against dist/: the BIP84 address with profiles ['legacy'] passes the check and never matches, while ['native-segwit'] matches. A long search then reports 'not matched' for every candidate instead of refusing the evidence before any secret is typed (src/core/wallet-evidence.ts:697, 630).
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: evidence of an address type outside the selected profiles is refused before any secret, with a new code; the wallet-tools session is told.

defects.defect: LocatedEvidence.compare derives the branch key and every scanned child in every selected profile, even for 'address' evidence, where only the profile of the address's own type can match. That is up to 4x wasted BIP32 derivations per candidate, which also inflates the search-time estimates (src/core/wallet-evidence.ts:652).
defects.how: Address evidence derives only in the profile its address type belongs to; results are the same, with fewer derivations and a truer time estimate.

defects.defect: --account-xpub accepts --branch and --index, validates them, then silently ignores them. Place options beside a master fingerprint or master xpub are refused precisely because they 'would be ignored' (src/cli/bitcoin-options.ts:211, src/core/wallet-evidence.ts:679).
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: --branch and --index beside --account-xpub are refused, as beside the master evidence.

defects.defect: The list passphrase (parseListPassphrase) and the Scanner recipient (parseRecipient) are trimmed with String.prototype.trim instead of the shared trimWhiteSpace, which follows Rust str::trim. The two differ on U+0085 and U+FEFF, so a Rust writer and a TypeScript reader can disagree on a list passphrase (src/core/candidate-encryption.ts:71, src/core/candidate-cipher.ts:168).
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed with the trimming defect: the list passphrase and the recipient are trimmed by the one rule.

defects.defect: --bip39-passphrase-file keeps a leading byte order mark, while the WIF file and the list-passphrase file strip it. A BOM added by an editor silently selects another wallet (src/cli/bitcoin-options.ts:228).
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): kept, since stripping it would select another wallet for an existing file; the program warns when the file starts with U+FEFF (TS first).

defects.defect: Bip39Seed raises 'Invalid mnemonic' only for a wrong word count. It does not check the words or the checksum, so the public entry points masterFingerprint and matchWalletEvidence derive a seed from any 12-word text. This matches @scure/bip39 mnemonicToSeed but is misleading for a library entry (src/core/master-fingerprint.ts:93).
defects.how: Seed derivation takes a validated Phrase, so no unvalidated text reaches it from any entry.

defects.defect: CORE-54: CandidateEncryption's gate keeps failure epochs, recheck barriers and retires results when a recheck fails mid-operation. This defends against the runtime changing its own known answers during a session, which nothing can cause; a check-once gate with an explicit recheck is enough (src/core/candidate-encryption.ts:111-348).
defects.how: candidates::gate checks the known answers once per process and on an explicit recheck; no epochs, barriers or retired results.

defects.defect: CORE-54: the guard 'dates-found-do-not-decode-codes-wallet-matched' re-decodes found codes only to catch a disagreement between MnemoCode's own date search and its own decoder (src/core/missing-codes-search.ts:858).
defects.how: The re-decode guard is not written: the date search and the decoder are the program's own code (CORE-54).

defects.defect: CORE-54: EncodedBackupCheck.#compareRestored runs after codes and dates were already found equal to the result's; its own comment says only a fault of MnemoCode can give a finding there (src/core/backup-check.ts:503).
defects.how: The final comparison is not written (CORE-54).

defects.defect: CORE-54: CandidatesFile.#save throws TooManyForListError for the outcome 'full', which its comment calls only a fault of MnemoCode, since the searches refuse earlier (src/cli/candidates-file.ts:231).
defects.how: The searches bound their counts before any secret, so the writer has no 'full' outcome to refuse.

defects.defect: CORE-54: several redundant guards. address-scan publicKeyOf has a null check (unable-derive-public-key) that a private HDKey cannot trigger. scanBranch re-runs addressCount on ranges its callers checked, and Coin.branchPathsOf re-checks a location CoinAddressComparison already checked. DateSearch.pace re-asserts the word count of its own copy. equalKeyBytes handles null keys that parsed or derived HDKeys always have. The DatesAnswer constructor's try/catch wipes earlier SecretValues if a later allocation of its own fails.
defects.how: Derived keys are typed and always present; ranges are checked once at the boundary (CORE-48) and not again inside.

defects.defect: CORE-22: CandidateFileAdmission.#lock throws its own code core.candidate-file-admission.invalid-supported-header and catches it at once to rethrow header-malformed. This is control flow by exception, and the code never reaches a host (src/core/candidate-file-admission.ts:247-260).
defects.how: Admission returns header-malformed directly; no error is thrown to be caught.

defects.defect: CORE-23: two ErrorCatalogs share the prefix core.candidates (candidates.ts and word-candidate.ts), and two share core.words (words.ts and word-table.ts). Nearby, core.dates has the non-descriptive pair assert-calendar-date-refused and assert-calendar-date-refused-2.
defects.how: A uniqueness test over every code of every enum (see the shared-namespace defect).

defects.defect: Not to be ported: wallet-check ownedAnswer walks the host answer's prototype chain and re-binds its methods and getters (AUD-016). This is JavaScript-host plumbing; a typed Rust wallet-check trait needs none of it.
defects.how: Not ported: evidence is data and WalletMatch a typed value; there is no host object to walk.

defects.defect: Documentation and code differ: docs/CANDIDATES.md says 'rich|rice' needs at least two words, but 'zoo|zoo' is accepted as a known place.
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed in the documents, TS first: 'zoo|zoo' stays accepted and CANDIDATES.md is corrected to the code (DOC-06).

defects.defect: The two defaults for addresses compared from a place are a trap: the library default is 1 when `addresses` is omitted, the command-line and screen default is 20. A host that relies on the library default compares a single address.
defects.how: wallet::scan takes the address count as a required argument and both front ends pass the one constant DEFAULT_SCAN_ADDRESSES (20); the library has no default.

defects.defect: Inconsistency: recover-word's legacy replacements call the wallet check directly (walletCheck?.(phrase)) instead of through askWallet, unlike every other search (src/cli/recover-word-command.ts:226).
defects.how: Every search, legacy replacements included, checks a candidate through the same evidence path; results are unchanged.

defects.defect: runtime.ts: the glue JS is hashed from one read but run through a separate import() (inside the single executable, from the bundle), so the pin does not bind the code that runs; integrity.json sits beside the files it pins, so only accidental corruption is caught
defects.how: No run-time loading: the engine is linked into the executable and the WASM; release integrity is the signed, reproducible artifact.

defects.defect: gf256.ts: sskr.gf256.zero-no-inverse-gf-256 can never fire, because gfInverse only receives xi^xj of points already proved distinct (CORE-54)
defects.how: The joint solver picks distinct members by construction; no zero-inverse guard.

defects.defect: gf256.ts: sskr.gf256.shamir-points-distinct cannot fire from its callers, because joint-solve baseOf always picks distinct members (CORE-54)
defects.how: No distinct-points guard; the callers' construction guarantees it.

defects.defect: bridge.ts:164-166: re-checks with byte-array-required that three arrays the function itself just pushed exist (CORE-54)
defects.how: The bridge passes typed slices; no re-check of arrays it built.

defects.defect: runtime.ts: sskr.runtime.bundle-reader type-checks a typed parameter whose only caller passes the default (CORE-54)
defects.how: No bundle reader exists.

defects.defect: split.ts: the checks of the engine's output (unexpected-share-count, another-split-than-asked, did-not-reconstruct-source-entropy) and randomness-left-seed-unfilled guard the program's own pinned engine and the OS CSPRNG; only a foreign host platform can trigger them (CORE-54, borderline; at most keep the restore check)
defects.how: The engine output checks and the 'randomness left unfilled' check are dropped (CORE-54); the restore of every new split is kept as the product's promise that written shares restore, like the QR read-back.

defects.defect: repair.ts: repairCandidates and its freeBits budget (0..8, default 4) are documented as library API in docs/SSKR.md, but no package entry exports them; sskr.repair.free-bits-budget is reachable only from the self-test
defects.how: repair candidates and the free-bits budget are pub(crate); the repository's SSKR document lists only public API.

defects.defect: cli/share-repair.ts:163: TypedShares.given reads values(args, 'share'), but --share is always refused on argv before parsing, so this path is dead
defects.how: --share is refused before parsing and no code reads share values from arguments.

defects.defect: The engine's Bytewords encoding (create_sskr_shares_formatted / recover_sskr_shares_formatted with code 1) is used by no MnemoCode path; TypeScript writes and reads Bytewords itself, so there are two implementations of Bytewords
defects.how: The bridge calls only the binary share functions; Bytewords has one implementation, sskr::forms::bytewords.

defects.defect: The TypeScript and Rust share readers disagree: TypeScript accepts a CBOR tag inside a UR, a non-shortest 0x58 byte-string head and, through JS 'iu' case folding, U+212A KELVIN SIGN as k anywhere and U+017F LONG S as s in the 'ur:sskr/' prefix; Rust refuses all of these. TypeScript canonicalises before the engine, so the looser rule wins end to end
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): kept: one Rust reader reproduces the looser TS 0.1.0 acceptance, so a share the TS reads, another tool's included, still restores; the engine checks every share.

defects.defect: --format means the share form in sskr-split and sskr-export, but the complete masked backup in encode --sskr, where --share-format is the share form: one option with two meanings
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): kept: renaming options breaks the scripts and documents that use them.

defects.defect: share_text.rs: u64::try_from(len).unwrap_or(u64::MAX) and u8::try_from(index).ok() over the 256-word list guard cases that cannot happen (CORE-54, minor)
defects.how: The bridge holds no such conversions; lengths are typed.

defects.defect: transport.ts readShare: a damaged Unicode-code share is refused with the colour reader's message, because colours come first among the hex forms
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: the refusal names the reader of the form the text is written in.

defects.defect: transport.ts MAX_COLOR_TEXT_LENGTH (1024) counts numbers for word numbers but UTF-16 characters for colours and Unicode codes: inconsistent unit
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): kept: each limit a named constant with its unit in its name; the limits bound input, and one unit would change nothing a person sees.

defects.defect: Inconsistent: --card-qr is silently ignored for share cards with --card-layout individual (no QR drawn, no refusal), while business-size seed-phrase cards refuse it (export.content-kinds.qr-code-printed-on-sheet-only-choose-size); src/export/sskr-render.ts:218
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: --card-qr with individual share cards is refused before any secret, as for business-size seed-phrase cards.

defects.defect: CLI/library gap: ShareCardSet accepts a sheet title, but no share command offers --title (sskr-split refuses it in SSKR mode, SSKR_EXPORT_OPTIONS lacks it)
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): kept: adding the option is a feature, not a fix (CORE-54).

defects.defect: NoCardTemplateError for a kind not in CARD_KIND_NAMES prints 'supports undefined cards'; the error and the CLI's noCardTemplateMessage/card-template-refused path are unreachable with the fixed 13-design catalog (src/export/template-catalog.ts:163)
defects.how: The card kind is an enum with one value; the no-template error and its CLI wrapper cannot occur and are dropped.

defects.defect: QR PNG export uses a 1-module quiet zone (qrcode margin: 1, src/export/qr-image.ts:31) while printed QR codes use the ISO/IEC 18004 4-module zone
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: the ISO/IEC 18004 4-module quiet zone, so saved and printed QR codes scan reliably; the QR known answers change.

defects.defect: Material sample choice uses unrounded Math.cbrt/Math.hypot (src/export/material-artwork.ts:512,632), so decorative samples may differ between JS engines, contrary to card-palette.ts's rule of rounding to millionths for engine independence
defects.how: Colour maths uses libm, the same on every host and target; any difference from V8's Math.cbrt in a decorative sample falls under the page-image tolerance (PLAN, "Parity with TS 0.1.0").

defects.defect: MIN_MODULE_MM = 0.4 (src/export/card-qr.ts:17) is a default only tests use; every production caller passes 0.3 mm
defects.how: One constant, the production 0.3 mm; no unused default.

defects.defect: colorCardsFit skips Unicode-code cards (format 3) and Encode runs it only with --ask-secrets, so a typed detail too long for its card is refused at save time after the result is shown (src/cli/cards-fit.ts:41, src/cli/encode-command.ts:174)
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: every form's fit, Unicode-code cards included, is checked before any secret.

defects.defect: sskr-export without --format checks printability in colors only; Unicode shares with material-enclosure or material-tile (32/27 samples < 33 codes) are refused only after the shares are typed
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: the chosen share form's own cards are checked before the shares are typed.

defects.defect: Two hide markers for a design text: '-' via CLI/overrides, '' via a host's whole presentation (checkedCardPresentation)
defects.how: The library API has one Hidden value; the CLI's '-' and a host's empty text both map to it in the front ends.

defects.defect: Preview plans decoys separately for its PDF and its page images (encode and shares share one plan)
defects.how: Preview draws its PDF and its images from one plan and one scene.

defects.defect: renderHeirSheet does not check the font's character set; a host route with characters outside the DejaVu subset fails with pdf-lib's own uncoded error
defects.how: Decided with the 25 (2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: the heir sheet checks its text against the font subset's character map before drawing and refuses with a new code of its catalog.

defects.defect: CORE-54 (guard against nothing): export.card-session.card-session-no-name (own state, comment admits it)
defects.how: No such guard: the session's state is typed.

defects.defect: CORE-54: export.collection-sheet.missing-design-study-qr-area cannot occur (layout is computed with the same QR matrix that is drawn)
defects.how: The layout is computed from the drawn matrix in one function; no missing-area guard.

defects.defect: CORE-54: export.collection-layout.invalid-design-study-layout appears unreachable (constant aspects; empty content refused earlier by the content check)
defects.how: Not written (constant aspects; content refused earlier).

defects.defect: CORE-54: export.card-decoys.cards-their-decoys-already unreachable (withPlannedDecoys handles counted decoys before withDecoyPool; module is no package entry)
defects.how: Not written (counted decoys handled first).

defects.defect: CORE-54: readRenderAsset's export.platform.unknown-card-asset only ever checks the program's own constant paths
defects.how: Assets are compiled-in constants; no allowlist check.

defects.defect: CORE-54: export.card-values.shape TypeError check; CardValues is constructed only from typed internal values
defects.how: CardValues is built only from typed values; no shape check.

defects.defect: CORE-54: export.export-details.snapshot-keys; the only caller passes objects and WeakMap already throws
defects.how: No snapshot-keys check; the type system holds the shape.

defects.defect: CORE-54: empty-catalog guards (CardPreview.jobs selectTemplate() call, preview's 'No card designs are installed.')
defects.how: The template registry is a non-empty constant list (a unit test); no empty-catalog guard.

defects.defect: CORE-54: export.qr-image.qr-payload-not-empty reachable only from the self-test's deliberate call
defects.how: The payload type is non-empty by construction; the self-test case is dropped.

defects.defect: CORE-54: cli.qr-input.qr-decoder-unavailable typeof check on a bundled dependency's export
defects.how: rqrr is linked; no run-time check of a decoder function.

defects.defect: CORE-54: EncodeCardExport shares a pending plan for a re-entrant host callback that the sequential CLI never makes; it also uses an empty SecretValue only as a liveness flag
defects.how: Each export holds its own plan by value; no shared pending plan and no empty owner used as a flag.

defects.defect: CORE-54 owner decision: every QR matrix from qrcode is rasterised and decoded with jsQR before drawing (QrPngReader.checkedModules) - guards a dependency, a cause CORE-54 does not name, but documented as a product promise
defects.how: Kept as the owner's product promise: qr verifies every matrix by drawing and decoding it with rqrr before it is drawn or saved.

defects.defect: ExportDetails re-settles complete profiles and still consumes random choices (createCardIdentity picks a sector even with a given company) only to keep fixed-seed test output; a port need not copy it
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): kept, so fixed-seed outputs stay byte-equal; a leaner order changes nothing a person sees.

defects.defect: Security note: separate-card file names contain the printed secret code ('01-ABCDEF.pdf'), exposing codes in directory listings and file metadata (documented behaviour)
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: separate-card file names carry the card's number, not its code, and the documents say so.

defects.defect: Dead secret-value paths: argv refuses --mnemonic/--input/--share/--date/--dates/--old-date/--old-dates/--last-word before parsing (src/cli/arguments.ts:51, src/cli/command-line.ts:84), but code still reads their values: textInput direct text (src/cli/input.ts:74), dateInputText (src/cli/input.ts:272), share values (src/cli/share-repair.ts:163), the --dates/--old-dates list branch and flagOf (src/cli/arguments.ts:106,145)
defects.how: The secret flags are refused before parsing and no code reads their values; the dead branches are not written.

defects.defect: Misleading refusal: cli.input.provide-as-direct-text-file-through-ask-secrets offers 'direct text', which is always refused (src/cli/input.ts:50); provide-either-as-direct-text-file-but-not cannot happen from the command line
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): fixed, TS first: the message no longer offers direct text.

defects.defect: CORE-54 guards against failures nobody can cause: cli.ask.question-after-failure-choice (src/cli/ask.ts:306), cli.ask.answer-question-stop-value (src/cli/ask.ts:351), cli.input-bytes.byte (src/cli/input-bytes.ts:23), cli.protection.mnemo-code-could-not-find-own-program-file (src/cli/protection.ts:97), core.defined.missing-value everywhere (src/core/defined.ts), cli.candidates-file.wiped (src/cli/candidates-file.ts:154), the rethrow of non-TypeError in strictUtf8Text (src/core/utf8-text.ts:27)
defects.how: None of these guards is written (CORE-54).

defects.defect: Cleanup written as more than one attempt: readLine nests try/finally so readAgain.wipe() runs if answer.wipe() throws, but fill(0) cannot throw (src/cli/terminal-input.ts:650-652)
defects.how: Wiping is Drop, one attempt; no nested cleanup.

defects.defect: swap-check encrypted() stops at depth 8 for a loop in /sys that the kernel cannot produce (src/cli/swap-check.ts:101)
defects.how: No depth limit: the device walk follows what the kernel lists, which has no loops.

defects.defect: One error namespace in two modules: share-repair.ts declares a second catalog 'cli.sskr-restore-command' (src/cli/share-repair.ts:78); the core module utf8-text.ts uses namespace 'cli.utf8' (src/core/utf8-text.ts:4)
defects.how: Each module's own enum carries its TS codes; a module never shares an enum with another; the uniqueness test covers the codes.

defects.defect: Codes outside ErrorCatalog with bare names and messages built in their classes (CORE-23): UnusableAnswerError answer-too-long/answer-not-utf8 (src/cli/typed-answer.ts:27), InputTooLargeError too-large (src/core/byte-units.ts:10), the private-file error classes left-staging-copy etc. (src/export/private-file.ts:49)
defects.how: These codes become variants of their modules' enums with their TS strings kept (RUST-14); their messages come from Display like every other.

defects.defect: Overloaded option names: --format is the code form in encode/decode/re-encode/recover-date but the share form in sskr-split/sskr-export, while encode --sskr calls that --share-format; --index is a word number (table) and an address index (wallet); --words, --all and --output each have two or three meanings
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): kept: renaming options breaks the scripts and documents that use them.

defects.defect: Only SIGINT is handled (src/cli/interruption.ts:33). SIGHUP (terminal closed), SIGTERM, and SIGQUIT (Ctrl+\ between questions) end the process without leaving the alternate screen or removing private staging folders, which may hold a copy of a secret export
defects.how: SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT (and the Windows console handler) restore the terminal, leave the private screen and remove staging folders; SIGTSTP restores the terminal, leaves the private screen and stops, and on continue the private screen and raw mode come back (N-SIGNALS).

defects.defect: Menu echo-off depends on /bin/stty (src/cli/menu-runner.ts:18). Where it is missing, echo silently stays on, so keys typed early can reach the scrollback
defects.how: Echo is switched off through termios or the console API directly; no /bin/stty.

defects.defect: ProgressLine truncates by UTF-16 length rather than display width (src/cli/terminal.ts:399)
defects.how: The progress line is cut by display cells (the same cell-width rule as the layout).

defects.defect: preflightFileDestination(path, allowOverwrite) never overwrites. true only means 'existing is fine, it will be numbered' (src/cli/output-paths.ts:266)
defects.how: The preflight's parameter is named for what it does (number an existing name), and it never overwrites.

defects.defect: Rights are dropped from options before assertAllowedArguments validates them (src/cli/command-line.ts:120-125); harmless but misordered
defects.how: Options are validated first, then the protections are applied for the validated needs; there is no permission model.

defects.defect: Inconsistent sandbox labels: Windows uses 'Windows: no other programs' (src/cli/sandbox-windows.ts:189), while Linux and macOS use 'kernel: ...' and 'sandbox: ...', and verify-executable.mjs matches these strings
defects.how: Decided (owner, 2026-10-27): kept: verify-executable matches the labels, and they change no protection. The Rust port prints no 'no other programs' label, since it denies no program start (owner, 2026-10-27).

defects.defect: Unwipeable string copies of shown and read secrets (a JS limitation, do not copy): PrivatePage.text() decodes the page on each repaint (src/cli/private-page.ts:79), and file and typed secrets become strings (text-file.ts, bitcoin-options.ts:232)
defects.how: Shown and read secrets stay in locked owners; a repaint writes from the owner to the terminal without a String copy.

defects.defect: Over-built: build-executable.mjs backs up the previous release set and rolls back renames with PublicationRollbackError (scripts/build-executable.mjs:180-210) for an output that can simply be rebuilt into a fresh folder
defects.how: Executables are built into a fresh folder; no backup or rollback.
